target_customer: Operators of critical infrastructure such as data centers, power grids, refineries, airports and military bases
problem: Legacy air defense effectors cost $1M or more per shot against drones costing about $30k, and critical sites lack cheap, always-ready protection.
business_model: Subscription: Air Defense as a Service including hardware, reloads and monitoring
product_category: Autonomous counter-drone interceptors in containerized launch units

founders.name: Jasper Lortije
previous_startups: Dutch GNSS-denied visual navigation company (per launch post)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he built a VTOL drone that won a Hannover Messe competition and worked with special forces on the counter-drone plan for the 2025 NATO Summit.

founders.name: Alessandro Fiume
founders.background_notes: Sales and operations; YC page credits him with the pipeline behind 180M+ USD in letters of intent.

competitors.name: Cambridge Aerospace (Skyhammer)
competitors.what: Low-cost interceptor UAV against Shahed-style drones
competitors.traction_then: UK and Gulf states ordered Skyhammer on 2026-04-10; UK contract reported near $6.5M
competitors.funding_then: A $200M round at $1.3B valuation reported earlier in 2026 (timing uncertain)

technical_complexity.rationale: Autonomous interception with GPS-denied vision guidance, sensor cueing and sealed launch containers, built by a two-person team. The company claims a SABLE jet prototype built in two weeks (August 2026), which is self-reported.

defensibility.rationale: Many funded interceptor makers exist. Moat could come from defense approvals and installed sites, but none is established yet.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Well-funded interceptor makers had government orders by April 2026; IMPACT launched in August 2026 and its outcome is unknown.

market_need_then: Shahed-class drones were hitting infrastructure and governments were buying cheap interceptors. The company cites 180M+ USD in signed letters of intent, which are non-binding and self-reported; pilots were planned from Q3 2026.

branding.domain_note: Uses impact-drones.com, a hyphenated descriptive domain

identity.visual_style: Cinematic and minimal with imagery of the container in real settings
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and declarative, e.g. 'Protect the grid.' and 'Nothing for you to operate.'

branding.brand_signature: Interceptor product names WEAVER, HUNTER and SABLE
branding.community_and_virality: Trade press coverage of the launch (Aviation Week, EDR, Defence Blog, The Defense Post)

brand_strength.rationale: Coverage of the launch and the SABLE prototype in defense trade outlets, a memorable product-name family, but a generic company name.

outcome_analysis: IMPACT is a two-person Summer 2026 defense hardware startup that launched Air Defense as a Service on 2026-08-04 and drew trade press. Reported demand consists of non-binding letters of intent, and no equity funding was verified. It faces well-funded interceptor competitors, so the outcome is too early to assess.
notes: Dealroom lists a $125k seed, an aggregator figure seen once, not recorded as a round. EDR Magazine returned 403 and was not worked around. Nordic9 describes a Dutch startup with an Amsterdam office while YC says San Francisco or Los Angeles; unresolved. Cambridge Aerospace funding dates in the source are inconsistent. Launch date 2026-08-04 comes from search summaries of trade press.
